result.journal: Transactions of the Institute of Measurement and Control
result.keywords: This paper addresses distributed fair-rate coordination for leader-following heterogeneous multi-agent systems under nonlinear dynamics and flow-control constraints. A distributed adaptive iterative learning framework is developed to regulate consensus tracking while preserving max-min fairness across agents with different dynamics. The model considers mixed first-order and second-order nonlinear subsystems, with only a subset of agents receiving leader information. Radial basis function neural networks are used to approximate nonlinear terms, and adaptive update laws are proposed for time-varying parameters. Theoretical analysis shows that the proposed protocols achieve stable tracking and fairness guarantees over both the time domain and iterative domain, and a numerical simulation illustrates the effectiveness of the method.
result.title: Distributed adaptive fair-rate learning for heterogeneous multi-agent flow control
